case.title: Profound deafness in a child whose parents are cousins
case.brief:
Referral from audiology. A boy of 3 has had bilateral profound sensorineural hearing loss since birth and has cochlear implants. His inner ears are normal on CT and MRI, and he is otherwise well. His parents are first cousins with normal hearing; his older sister is also profoundly deaf, and his baby brother hears normally.

A hearing-loss gene panel found GJB2 NM_004004.6:c.35del p.(Gly12ValfsTer2), homozygous. Both parents and his brother are heterozygous; his sister is homozygous.
tasks: How common is this variant in gnomAD? Use the frequency calculator for a recessive disorder: is it too common to cause profound deafness? What do BA1 and BS1 say, and why are there exceptions?
PVS1: GJB2’s protein is coded by one exon, so nonsense-mediated decay does not apply. Work through the decision tree.
Draw on the pedigree: what does the consanguinity explain? Do the siblings’ results add segregation evidence?
Classify, sign and compare with the ClinGen Hearing Loss expert panel.
case.source: Variant: NM_004004.6(GJB2):c.35del, GRCh38 13-20189546-AC-A, ClinGen allele CA127023. ClinVar VCV000017004; ClinGen Hearing Loss VCEP classification (Evidence Repository). Checked October 2026. The patient and family are fictional.

patients.ref: Case 6: child with profound congenital deafness whose parents are cousins
patients.referral: Audiology: bilateral profound sensorineural hearing loss from birth (failed newborn hearing screen); cochlear implants at 14 months.
patients.summary: Boy of 3 with bilateral profound congenital sensorineural hearing loss, otherwise well. CT and MRI of the inner ears normal. No goitre, no balance problems, normal ECG.
patients.familyHistory: Parents are first cousins, both with normal hearing. Older sister (6) has the same profound deafness; younger brother (9 months) passed his newborn hearing screen and hears normally. Parents and siblings tested: both parents and the brother are heterozygous, the sister is homozygous.

phenotypes.name: Abnormality of the inner ear
phenotypes.note: CT and MRI of the inner ears normal

patients.notes: Fictional patient and family; the variant and the published evidence about it are real.

expected.source: ClinGen Hearing Loss expert panel (VCEP), Evidence Repository; ClinVar VCV000017004 (Pathogenic, reviewed by expert panel, 2018-09-20).

notes.PVS1: GJB2 has a single coding exon and loss of function is the well-known mechanism: a frameshift at codon 12 removes almost all of the protein.
notes.PS4: Far commoner in people with hearing loss than in controls: about 37% of European hearing-loss alleles in a meta-analysis of 52 studies, against under 1% of gnomAD’s European alleles.
notes.PM3: Very strong: more than 15 people homozygous, or compound heterozygous with other pathogenic GJB2 variants, in a single published series.
notes.BA1: Met by the frequency (a filtering allele frequency of 0.92% when the panel curated it, 0.81% in gnomAD v4.1: above the panel’s BA1 threshold of 0.5% for recessive hearing loss) but not counted: the variant is on the panel’s list of exceptions, as GJB2 c.109G>A is on ClinGen’s general list. A pathogenic variant of a recessive disorder can be common, because carriers are well.
notes.BS1: Not met, for the same reason (the panel’s BS1 threshold for recessive hearing loss is 0.3%).
notes.PM2: Not met: common in gnomAD (about 0.8% of European alleles).
notes.PP1: Not applied by the panel. In this family the affected sister is homozygous and the hearing brother is not: a likelihood ratio of about 5, moderate by Tavtigian’s odds but fewer than 3 meioses by counting. It would not change the class.
